name: Discourse
description: Discourse is an open-source discussion and community platform for structured topics, replies, categories, tags, groups, moderation, messaging, and knowledge sharing.
agentUseSummary: Connect a dedicated customer-owned API key, one exact API username, and one exact public HTTPS Discourse site. Agents can inspect reduced site, actor, Category, Tag, Group, member, and latest Topic metadata and make exact existing-username Group membership changes. Content, messaging, moderation, lifecycle, structural administration, bulk operations, private identity, and arbitrary API access remain blocked.

credentialRequirements.name: DISCOURSE_BASE_URL
credentialRequirements.label: Discourse site URL
credentialRequirements.helpText: Enter the public HTTPS origin of the exact Discourse site, without a path.

credentialRequirements.name: DISCOURSE_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Discourse API key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Create a dedicated single-user, least-privilege API key in Admin → Advanced → API Keys. Relay encrypts it and never exposes it to agents or clients after saving.

credentialRequirements.name: DISCOURSE_API_USERNAME
credentialRequirements.label: Discourse API username
credentialRequirements.helpText: Enter the exact username associated with the dedicated API key. Relay fixes this value in every Api-Username header.

blocked.label: Read or write content
blocked.description: Post bodies, excerpts, cooked HTML, drafts, private messages, chat, uploads, files, media, polls, events, forms, and arbitrary rich content are outside V1.

blocked.label: Manage user lifecycle
blocked.description: Creating, inviting, activating, approving, updating, anonymizing, suspending, silencing, deleting, impersonating, or changing trust and staff roles is outside V1.

blocked.label: Administer site structure
blocked.description: Creating, updating, deleting, reordering, or configuring Categories, Groups, Tags, Tag Groups, badges, themes, plugins, webhooks, settings, and site state is outside V1.

blocked.label: Moderate community content
blocked.description: Flagging, reviewing, deleting, moving, closing, pinning, archiving, hiding, locking, or otherwise moderating Topics, Posts, users, and reviewables is outside V1.

blocked.label: Communicate or notify
blocked.description: Creating Topics or Posts, private messaging, chat, email, invitations, notifications, broadcasts, and outbound webhooks are outside V1.

blocked.label: Run bulk or analytics actions
blocked.description: Automatic pagination, bulk loops, polling, exports, backups, logs, Data Explorer, analytics, IP data, email lookups, and staff audit data are outside V1.

blocked.label: Read broader identity data
blocked.description: Emails, secondary emails, IP addresses, avatars, profile fields, custom fields, timezones, last-seen activity, user statistics, and raw user or member records are outside V1.

blocked.label: Use arbitrary Discourse APIs
blocked.description: Arbitrary endpoints, methods, parameters, headers, bodies, alternate origins, API usernames, raw responses, plugins, GraphQL, CLI, and direct database access are outside V1.

evidence.supports: The official generated REST reference documents header authentication, site, Category, Tag, Tag Group, Group, Group member, latest Topic, and exact Group membership endpoints and schemas used by Relay's typed wrappers.
Discourse requires Api-Key and Api-Username HTTP headers and no longer supports general API credentials in query parameters or request bodies.

Administrators create API keys with a description, All Users or Single User binding, and Global, Read-only, or Granular scope; keys are displayed once, permissions cannot exceed the associated user, and unused keys can be revoked automatically.
Discourse supports route- and parameter-constrained API-key scopes, while endpoints absent from selected granular scopes fail closed.
Discourse publishes its generated OpenAPI source under the official discourse organization and derives it from core request specifications.
Discourse's legal portal governs hosted service terms while open-source installations remain subject to their own operator policies and licenses.
Discourse's privacy notice distinguishes hosted customer processing from each forum operator's privacy practices and describes the sensitivity of account, post, private-message, and activity data.
